ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in diamond ABCD, M and N are on AB and CD, respectively, and $AM = CN$, MN intersects AC at point O, connect $BO$, if $\angle DAC = 31^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle OBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
it follows that $AB\parallel CD$ and $AB=BC$,\\
therefore $\angle MAO=\angle NCO$ and $\angle AMO=\angle CNO$,\\
in $\triangle AMO$ and $\triangle CNO$,\\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle MAO=\angle NCO\hfill \\ AM=CN\hfill \\ \angle AMO=\angle CNO\hfill \end{array}\right.$,\\
it follows that $\triangle AMO \cong \triangle CNO\left(ASA\right)$,\\
therefore $AO=CO$,\\
since $AB=BC$,\\
it follows that $BO\perp AC$,\\
therefore $\angle BOC=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle DAC=31^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BCA=\angle DAC=31^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle OBC=90^\circ-31^\circ=\boxed{59^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a tilted rhombus, A is at the lower left, B is at the upper left, C is at the upper right, D is at the lower right; M is marked on side AB, N is marked on side CD; segment MN intersects diagonal AC at point O, and BO is connected in the figure. The problem gives AM = CN, and ∠DAC = 31°. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rhombus, AB ∥ CD, AD ∥ BC, and AB = BC. M is on AB, N is on CD, therefore AM ∥ CN. Also because O is on AC and O is on MN, AO and CO are collinear, MO and NO are collinear. Thus ∠MAO = ∠NCO, ∠AMO = ∠CNO. Combining AM = CN, it can be obtained that △AMO ≅ △CNO (ASA), so AO = CO, that is, O is the midpoint of AC. In △ABC, AB = BC, therefore it is an isosceles triangle with AC as the base; the segment BO from vertex B to the midpoint O of base AC is perpendicular to AC, so ∠BOC = 90°. Also because AD ∥ BC, and A, O, C are collinear, ∠BCA = ∠DAC = 31°, that is, ∠OCB = 31°. In right triangle BOC, ∠OBC = 90° − 31° = 59°.
